panel.label: Mission figures
metrics.help.sunlight: Hours within the mission when the Sun's centre is above the real horizon, seen from 2 m above the ground. Source: JPL DE440 ephemeris and LOLA terrain.
metrics.help.earth_link: Hours with the Earth's centre above the real horizon: a direct line of sight for radio contact. It does not model antennas or ground stations.
metrics.help.longest_night: Longest continuous period without the Sun during the mission. By default a site passes if no night lasts over 24 h: a team default, not a mission rule. Change it in Setup › Requirements or in Replan (0–400 h).
power.figures_label: Power and communications estimate for the mission
power.energy_sub: {total} kWh in the mission · peak {peak} W
power.link_sub: {pct} % of the mission · longest gap {gap} h
power.notice: Estimate, not a mission design: {area} m² panel, {eff} % efficient, {orient} · {load} W load at night · link with the Earth ≥ {min}° above the real horizon · no dust, heat, wiring or battery losses.
power.orient_vertical: vertical, turned to face the Sun
power.f_min: Minimum Earth elevation above the real horizon (°)
power.sources: Solar constant 1361 W/m² (Kopp & Lean 2011), scaled by the Sun's distance; 30.7 % efficiency of a triple-junction space cell (Spectrolab XTJ Prime datasheet, beginning of life, AM0). 1 m² and 100 W are reference units: results scale with them.
limits.rise_set: Rise and set times are only as accurate as the terrain map. Where the horizon is set by low relief close to the site, a few metres of error in the map shift them by tens of minutes at mid-latitudes and by hours near the poles, where the Sun skims the horizon.
metrics.outside: The cursor is outside the ephemeris table.

timeline.no_events: No sunrise, sunset, Earthrise or Earthset during the mission.
validation.title: How we know the numbers are right
validation.none: Validation report not available in this build.
validation.a7b7_rule: NASA counts a point as lit when any part of the Sun's or Earth's disc is visible; this comparison uses the same rule. The app's own layers use the disc centre.
validation.no_details: No detailed values for this check.
validation.footer: Generated from the automated test report · commit {commit}

replan.intro: When could you land, and where? Each row is a site: your scenarios, and NASA's candidate regions if you tick the box. Each column is a later landing: +0 is the planned date ({date}), +1 d one day later, and so on. Set the requirements and the delay step, then pick a cell to use that date.
